title: Chicken Tikka Masala
shortDescription: Rich curry on a busy night
subtitle: Rich curry on a busy night
description: Rich curry on a busy night. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Cook basmati for the line
steps.instruction: Rinse basmati; simmer 1:1.5 with salted water 15 minutes. Rest covered 10 minutes, fluff, and hold at 200°F. Basmati should stay separate — not sticky mush.

steps.title: Mix tikka marinade
steps.instruction: Stir yogurt with paprika, cumin, half the garam masala, garlic, ginger, and salt. Coat chicken; refrigerate at least 45 minutes.

steps.title: Char the chicken
steps.instruction: Broil on racks 6 inches from heat or grill over medium-high until edges char and centers hit 165°F. Work in batches so pieces char instead of steam.

steps.title: Hold charred chicken
steps.instruction: Rest charred chicken 5 minutes; hold loosely covered at 140°F while the sauce finishes.

steps.title: Start the masala base
steps.instruction: Sweat onion in oil over medium heat 8–10 minutes until edges turn gold. Add remaining garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer tomato and cream
steps.instruction: Add crushed tomatoes and remaining garam masala; simmer 12 minutes until the sauce thickens and oil sheen appears at the edges. Stir in cream; simmer 5 minutes without a hard boil.

steps.title: Fold in chicken
steps.instruction: Add charred chicken and resting juices. Simmer gently 10 minutes so flavors marry. Sauce should look coral-orange and coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.instruction: Balance with salt and a squeeze of lemon if the sauce tastes flat. Add a splash of cream if spice reads too sharp for the crew.

steps.title: Serve Chicken Tikka Masala
steps.instruction: Plate rice first, then ladle masala over top with cilantro. Keep naan or flatbread on a side tray if the hall stocks it.

steps.title: Hold and store safely
steps.instruction: If interrupted, hold covered at 140°F. Cool leftovers shallow within two hours; reheat to 165°F before the next meal.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Tikka Masala with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Tikka Masala on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Rich curry on a busy night. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
